original_question: What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations?
target_in_paper: Section 2, under “Open problems,” fourth bullet (p. 4): "What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations ?" This is the exact official formulation your draft is aiming at. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to perfect paper-faithfulness: it matches the exact open problem the authors state, and it correctly focuses on vanishing, on Nambu micro-graphs rather than arbitrary Poisson-graph expressions, and on both single graphs and linear combinations. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
missing_details: The ambient setting is the family of Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets on R^d, for d >= 3 in the open-problem list, given by {f,g}_d(x) = rho(x) det(partial(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2}) / partial(x_1,...,x_d)), with Casimirs a_i in C^1(R^d); the draft does not state this background. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

A Nambu micro-graph is not an arbitrary digraph: it is built from whole copies of bracket (1), with m sinks and n Levi-Civita vertices together with their attached Casimir vertices; the draft does not define the object class. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The paper’s notion of vanishing is formula-level vanishing: the differential-polynomial expression encoded by the graph calculus, written as phi(Gamma), is identically zero. The draft leaves “vanishing” informal. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The relevant linear combinations are R-linear combinations of Nambu micro-graphs; the paper explicitly allows such combinations and notes that not every such combination is itself a Kontsevich graph. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

Because the sign is essential, one should note that each Levi-Civita vertex carries an ordered tuple of outgoing edges; this ordered structure is what allows an automorphism to force Gamma = -Gamma in some cases. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The nearby context isolates two observed cancellation patterns motivating the question: self-negation under an automorphism, and pairwise cancellation of terms even when Aut(Gamma) = {1}. The draft does not mention these already-detected mechanisms. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

The scope is the Nambu side of Kontsevich’s tetrahedral cocycle flow, motivated in particular by the vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs used when trying to trivialize that flow in dimension shifts d -> d+1; the draft omits this paper-specific motivation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))

No homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, characteristic, or “for all sufficiently large m” qualifier belongs to this statement; a stand-alone version should make the setting precise without adding such extra hypotheses. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
refined_question: In the setting of Kontsevich’s tetrahedral graph-cocycle flow on the Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets {f,g}_d(x)=rho(x) det(partial(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2})/partial(x_1,...,x_d)) on R^d for d >= 3, determine a conceptual criterion, expressed in terms of the automorphism group and the topology of the underlying directed Nambu micro-graph, that explains exactly when a Nambu micro-graph Gamma built from whole copies of bracket (1), or an R-linear combination of such micro-graphs, has identically vanishing encoded formula phi(Gamma)=0; in particular, account both for vanishing caused by an automorphism with Gamma congruent to -Gamma and for the symmetry-free pairwise cancellations observed for nonzero graphs with Aut(Gamma) = {1}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s exact fourth open problem in Section 2, so the right refinement is not to broaden it but to make it self-contained by importing the ambient Nambu-bracket formula, the definition of Nambu micro-graph, and the meaning of formula-level vanishing phi(Gamma)=0 from the introduction and preliminaries. I also made explicit the two concrete vanishing patterns the paper has already identified, because they are the immediate local context for the question. Proposition 1 is relevant nearby because it supports the authors’ claim that, in the studied 3D -> 4D step, no new vanishing mechanisms need be sought beyond descendants of earlier vanishing graphs, which is precisely why understanding the underlying mechanism matters. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.06121))
